about: A demo run, replayed from a live gpt-6-luna run (1015-140835-607f) at about 25x speed. The planner's question, every agent's edits and reports, and the checker model's rulings are that run's; in the live run the owner tried all ten model families, and here you choose. The tests, checks, merges and budget caps run for real on a fresh copy of repo/. Code identical to the live run's gets the score already measured for it, from scores.json (LUCIDITY_RESCORE=1 recomputes them all, about 3 minutes, mostly the SVM); any other code is scored for real. Agents were refused the held-out seasons; only Lucidity scored them. Game results are from FiveThirtyEight's NBA Elo data (CC BY 4.0).
title: NBA game forecasts

card.ask: Will the home team win? Using only what was known before tip-off.
card.why: FiveThirtyEight's published forecast for the same games, the best answer here without agents.

blurb: A model predicts the chance the home team wins an NBA game, using only what was known before tip-off. It scores 0.623 log loss; FiveThirtyEight's Elo forecast scores 0.608, so the goal is 0.6068. Ten kinds of model are tried at once, one agent each. Lucidity scores every attempt on two seasons the agents never see, checks each agent really built the model it was given, and recommends the best.
split: Trained on the 2001-2012 seasons, tuned on 2013, tested on 2014-2015. Agents never see the test seasons; only Lucidity scores them.

references.label: Coin flip (always 50%)
references.why: Say 50% for every row. Log loss charges 0.693 a row for that, so 0.693 means no skill at all.

references.label: Always guess the home team's usual win rate
references.why: Say the same chance, about 60%, for every home team.

references.label: Plain logistic regression (the starting model)
references.why: Ordinary logistic regression on both win-rate columns, no tuning.

references.label: FiveThirtyEight's forecast
references.why: FiveThirtyEight's published Elo forecast for the same games.

about_repo: bundled NBA win-probability model: 19,274 games 2001-2015, logistic regression, evals/score.py
commit_message: hoopkit: season win % + logistic regression, NBA games 2001-2015, evals/score.py
goal: Get held-out log loss to 0.6068 or lower (FiveThirtyEight's Elo forecast scores 0.608) without accuracy dropping. Tune on the dev split. Ask the owner which model families to try (plain linear regression with predictions clipped to 1-99%, plain logistic regression, naive Bayes, lasso logistic regression, ridge logistic regression, kNN, SVM, a single decision tree, random forest, boosted trees), any of them may use Elo-style team ratings built from earlier games as inputs, then build each one in parallel and keep the best. Give each agent up to 4 rounds.

plan.summary: Ask the owner which model families to try before work begins. Run the selected approaches in parallel; each attempt can tune on dev, and the final held-out evaluation gates the winning implementation at log loss ≤ 0.6068 with accuracy not below baseline.

nodes.title: Implement and dev-tune selected model families
nodes.prompt: For each family selected by the owner, implement a separate scikit-learn-shaped estimator path compatible with the repo's model/features interface. Tune using only the dev split; optional Elo-style team ratings must use earlier games only and preserve the tracker’s no-lookahead behavior. Compare candidates on dev log loss and accuracy, and retain the best viable candidate.
strategies: Plain linear regression (clip 1–99%). Build a linear regression classifier, converting its output to probabilities by clipping to [0.01, 0.99]; tune only on dev.
Plain logistic regression. Build and dev-tune standard logistic regression, including reasonable feature scaling where appropriate.
Naive Bayes. Build and dev-tune a suitable Naive Bayes classifier with any needed feature transformations.
Lasso logistic regression. Build and dev-tune logistic regression with L1 regularization, including regularization strength.
Ridge logistic regression. Build and dev-tune logistic regression with L2 regularization, including regularization strength.
kNN. Build a scaled k-nearest-neighbors classifier and dev-tune neighbor count and relevant distance settings.
SVM. Build and dev-tune a scaled SVM classifier with probability outputs or calibration.
Single decision tree. Build and dev-tune a single decision tree classifier, controlling depth and leaf size.
Random forest. Build and dev-tune a random forest classifier with sensible limits on depth and leaf size.
Boosted trees. Build and dev-tune a boosted-tree classifier using available project dependencies; constrain complexity to avoid overfit.

nodes.title: Validate final held-out performance
nodes.prompt: After model changes are complete, run the required held-out evaluation and report the JSON scores. If the chosen model misses the target or loses accuracy versus the starting held-out baseline, make only minimal fixes supported by dev evaluation and revalidate.

reviewer: The model that makes the predi.evidence: `make_model()` returns a pipeline ending in `LogisticRegression(penalty="l1", solver="liblinear", C=0.12, max_iter=1000)`; `StandardScaler` only scales inputs.

`make_model()` returns a pipeline of `StandardScaler()` and `LogisticRegression(penalty="l2", C=0.08, solver="lbfgs", max_iter=1000)`. The model making predictions is therefore L2-regularized logistic regression; feature additions do not replace or blend the estimator.
`make_model()` returns `RandomForestClassifier(...)`; the prediction path is not replaced by another estimator or a blend.
